newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude ends up on Iraq news, short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude ends up on Iraq news, short covering.

text.p: NYMEX crude prices ended with sharp gains Monday after Iraq's breach of a Western imposed "no-fly" zone was viewed as threatening the country's oil-for-food accord with the United Nations and prompted a bout of short covering.

There was also talk that Citgo had shut a 65,000 barrel per day (bpd) catalytic cracker at its 130,000 barrel per day Corpus Christi refinery, boosting refined product prices. Citgo officials declined comment.
May crude ended 47 cent a barrel up at $20.38. May gasoline ended 1.31 cents a gallon higher at 62.80 cents.
May heating oil settled 0.80 cent a gallon higher at 55.48 cents.
"I think the Iraqi news started us off today, and coupled with Citgo, things sort of blew up," said an oil dealer in Atlanta. But, refined products were seen mostly led by crude.
"I think Iraq (news) more than anything else helped us along with short covering in crude," said a New York gasoline dealer.
Both funds and local players scrambled to cover short positions in May crude ahead of the May crude contract expiry on Tuesday, dealers said.
